intro.en: Practical exam guide to the fetal skull and maternal pelvis models, detailing skull bones, sutures, fontanelles, obstetric diameters, pelvic planes, and pelvic architecture.

items.summary: An anatomical model of the neonatal fetal cranium demonstrating vault bones, sutures, fontanelles, landmarks, and engaging diameters.

blocks.title: Cranial bones of the fetal skull
bullets: Bony cranial plates enclose and safeguard the neonatal brain during transit through the maternal birth canal.
Frontal bones: Symmetrical halves forming the sinciput (forehead), joined by the frontal suture; fusion occurs by 8 years.
Parietal bones: Pair occupying the major lateral convexity of the vault between the frontal and occipital bones.
Occipital bone: Forms the posterior skull base and back of the head, articulating with parietals at the lambdoid suture.
Temporal bones: Lateral bones situated near the ears, adjacent to the inferior margins of the parietal bones.

groups.label: Primary cranial sutures
bullets: Frontal (metopic) suture: Runs along the midline between frontal bones from anterior fontanelle down to glabella.
Coronal suture: Transverse suture traversing from ear to ear, separating frontal bones from parietal bones.
Sagittal suture: Longitudinal midline suture uniting both parietal bones from bregma to lambda.
Lambdoid suture: Inverted V-shaped suture on posterior cranium separating parietals from occipital bone.

groups.label: Clinical importance of sutures
bullets: Permits slight bony mobility and cranial moulding during labour, accommodating symmetric brain growth.
Premature sutural fusion results in craniosynostosis and abnormal cranial morphology.
Vaginal suture palpation determines fetal station, position, cranial attitude (flexion), and internal rotation.
Transverse arrest of sagittal suture at the ischial spines establishes deep transverse arrest.
Sutures define boundaries that contain cephalhaematoma while permitting caput succedaneum to cross freely.

groups.label: Grading criteria
bullets: Moulding is the physiological alteration of cranial contour under birth-canal resistance; resolves within hours.
Grade 0: Cranial bones lie side by side separated by an intact intervening suture membrane.
Grade 1: Cranial bones touch edge to edge at the suture margins without overlapping.
Grade 2: Bones overlap at the suture line but are easily reducible with gentle digital pressure.
Grade 3: Bony overlap is firmly locked and irreducible with finger pressure.

groups.label: Clinical implications
bullets: Mild moulding (grades 1 and 2) is harmless and beneficial, facilitating passage through the pelvic canal.
Severe or irreducible moulding (grade 3) suggests cephalopelvic disproportion and increases intracranial trauma risk.

groups.label: Caput succedaneum characteristics
bullets: Present immediately at delivery following spontaneous vaginal birth; physiological in origin.
Localised scalp oedema caused by venous compression from the dilating cervix and introitus.
Soft, ill-defined swelling that pits on pressure and freely crosses cranial suture lines.
Lacks underlying skull bone fracture; maximal at birth and resolves spontaneously within 24 hours.

groups.label: Cephalhaematoma characteristics
bullets: Appears several hours (typically after 12 hours) or days following delivery, often after instrumental extraction.
Subperiosteal haemorrhage between skull bone and pericranium, strictly limited by sutural periosteal attachments.
Pathological swelling that is circumscribed, soft, and non-pitting; may enlarge over initial days.
May accompany an underlying skull fracture; resorbs slowly over 6 to 8 weeks, predisposing to neonatal jaundice.

groups.label: Anatomy and dimensions
bullets: Membranous gaps formed where sutures meet, covered by scalp skin and thick fibrous tissue.
Six fontanelles exist: anterior, posterior, two anterolateral (sphenoidal), and two posterolateral (mastoid).
Anterior fontanelle (Bregma): Diamond-shaped space with membranous floor at junction of frontal, coronal, sagittal sutures.
Bregma measures roughly 4 cm anteroposteriorly by 2.5 cm transversely; ossifies by 18 months of life.
Posterior fontanelle (Lambda): Triangular space with bony floor at junction of sagittal and lambdoid sutures.
Lambda ossifies physiologically by 2 to 3 months following birth.
Anterolateral (sphenoidal) fontanelles: Located between sphenoid, parietal, temporal, and frontal bones.
Posterolateral (mastoid) fontanelles: Located between temporal, occipital, and parietal bones.

groups.label: Clinical examination points
bullets: Digital fontanelle palpation identifies fetal presentation, position, degree of cranial flexion, and internal rotation.
Readily palpable posterior fontanelle verifies good vertex flexion; fontanelles also accommodate cranial moulding.
Bulging anterior fontanelle indicates elevated intracranial pressure in hydrocephalus, meningitis, and encephalitis.
Depressed or sunken anterior fontanelle is a physical hallmark of infantile dehydration and malnutrition.
Enlarged fontanelle occurs in Down syndrome, hydrocephalus, IUGR, neonatal hypothyroidism, and prematurity.
Rare causes of enlarged fontanelles include achondroplasia, cleidocranial dysostosis, congenital rubella, and rickets.

blocks.title: Anatomical landmarks of the fetal cranium
bullets: Vertex: Quadrate zone bounded by anterior fontanelle, posterior fontanelle, and lateral parietal eminences.
Vertex presentation is the standard, safest presentation for normal vaginal birth.
Brow: Cranial area extending from anterior fontanelle to supraorbital ridges; persistent brow cannot deliver vaginally.
Face: Cranial zone extending from supraorbital margins down to the chin (mentum).
Sinciput: Anterior cranial region corresponding to the fetal forehead.
Occiput: Area lying between the posterior fontanelle and the foramen magnum at the skull base.
Mentum: Anatomical midpoint of the fetal chin.
Subocciput: Junctional zone where the fetal neck joins the occiput beneath the external protuberance.
Submentum: Junction where the floor of the mouth joins the anterior neck.
Vertical point: Exact geometric midpoint of the sagittal suture.
Glabella: Bony prominence at the root of the nose, also designated the frontal point.
Parietal eminences: Prominent lateral bony tuberosities on the convexities of the parietal bones.

blocks.title: Longitudinal diameters of the fetal skull

groups.label: Sub-occipito bregmatic (SOB)
bullets: Extends from beneath the occipital protuberance to the centre of the anterior fontanelle.
Measures 9.5 cm; presents in complete flexion in vertex presentation; smallest engaging longitudinal diameter.

groups.label: Sub-occipito frontal (SOF)
bullets: Extends from beneath the occipital protuberance to the midpoint of the frontal suture.
Measures 10 cm; presents in incomplete flexion in vertex presentation.

groups.label: Occipito frontal (OF)
bullets: Extends from the occipital protuberance to the glabella (root of the nose).
Measures 11.5 cm; presents in marked deflexion (military attitude) in vertex presentation; causes prolonged labour.

groups.label: Mento-vertical (MV)
bullets: Extends from the mentum (midpoint of chin) to the vertex (centre of sagittal suture).
Measures 13.5 to 14 cm; presents in partial extension (brow presentation); delivery requires caesarean section.

groups.label: Sub-mento vertical (SMV)
bullets: Extends from the junction of the floor of the mouth and neck to the vertex.
Measures 11.5 cm; presents in incomplete extension in face presentation.

groups.label: Sub-mento bregmatic (SMB)
bullets: Extends from the junction of the floor of the mouth and neck to the bregma.
Measures 9.5 cm; presents in complete extension in face presentation; engagement is delayed, delivering by flexion.

blocks.title: Transverse diameters of the fetal skull

groups.label: Biparietal diameter
bullets: Extends between the two lateral parietal eminences; measures 9.5 cm.
Most favourable transverse diameter, almost universally engaging during normal cephalic labour.

groups.label: Super-subparietal diameter
bullets: Extends from above one parietal eminence to below the opposite eminence; measures 8.5 cm.
Engages as the presenting transverse diameter during asynclitic presentation.

groups.label: Bitemporal diameter
bullets: Extends between the inferior terminal points of the coronal sutures on either side; measures 8 cm.

groups.label: Bimastoid diameter
bullets: Extends between the tips of the mastoid processes; measures 7.5 cm.
Rigid and incompressible; if maternal bi-ischial diameter is 7.5 cm or less, vaginal delivery is impossible.

viva.q: What is the smallest engaging longitudinal diameter of the fetal skull and when does it present?
viva.a: The sub-occipito bregmatic diameter, measuring 9.5 cm, engages when the fetal head is completely flexed in a vertex presentation.

viva.q: Why is persistent brow presentation unable to deliver vaginally?
viva.a: The engaging diameter is the mento-vertical, measuring 13.5 to 14 cm, which greatly exceeds the maximum capacity of the maternal pelvis.

viva.q: How do you clinically distinguish caput succedaneum from cephalhaematoma?
viva.a: Caput succedaneum is present at birth, pits on pressure, and crosses suture lines. Cephalhaematoma appears hours later, does not pit, and is confined by sutures.

viva.q: What is the clinical significance of the bimastoid diameter?
viva.a: Measuring 7.5 cm, the bimastoid diameter is completely incompressible. If the maternal bi-ischial diameter is 7.5 cm or smaller, vaginal birth is impossible.

items.summary: An anatomical model of the articulated female bony pelvis demonstrating the pelvic inlet, cavity, outlet, landmarks, and obstetric diameters.
unsure: Source text notes calculating obstetric conjugate as 'diagonal conjugate 12 cm-2 cm' in narrative text, whereas its inlet table states the diagonal conjugate is 12.5 cm. Standard clinical practice calculates obstetric conjugate by subtracting 1.5 to 2 cm from the measured diagonal conjugate (12.5 cm - 2 cm = 10.5 cm or 10 cm).

blocks.title: Bones, joints, and divisions of the maternal pelvis

groups.label: Bones and articulating joints
bullets: Formed by four bones: two innominate (hip) bones, one sacrum, and one coccyx.
Connected by four joints: two sacroiliac joints, one sacrococcygeal joint, and the pubic symphysis.

groups.label: True pelvis versus false pelvis
bullets: False pelvis: Lies above the pelvic brim, bounded by anterior abdominal wall, lumbar vertebrae, and iliac fossae.
The false pelvis has minor obstetric significance aside from supporting the gravid uterus.
True pelvis: Bony canal below the pelvic brim bounded by pubic symphysis, sacrum, coccyx, and pelvic cavity.
The true pelvis forms the birth canal and is divided into three components: inlet, cavity, and outlet.

blocks.title: Pelvic inlet boundaries and architectural shapes

groups.label: Boundaries of the pelvic brim
bullets: Traced from posterior to anterior through 9 sequential anatomical landmarks.
Sacral promontory to sacral ala to sacroiliac joint to iliopectineal line.
Iliopectineal eminence to pectineal line / superior pubic ramus to pubic tubercle.
Pubic crest to the upper border of the pubic symphysis.
The plane of the inlet inclines at an angle of 55 degrees with the horizontal (angle of pelvic inclination).

groups.label: Inlet morphology in pelvic types
bullets: Gynaecoid pelvis: Typical female pelvis characterized by a rounded pelvic inlet.
Anthropoid pelvis: Features a longitudinally oval inlet with an elongated anteroposterior diameter.
Android pelvis: Male-type pelvis possessing a heart-shaped or triangular inlet with a narrow forepelvis.
Platypelloid pelvis: Flat pelvis featuring a transversely oval inlet with reduced anteroposterior dimension.

groups.label: Anteroposterior conjugates
bullets: Anatomical conjugate (true conjugate): Midpoint of sacral promontory to upper border of symphysis pubis; measures 11 cm.
Obstetric conjugate: Midpoint of sacral promontory to prominent bulge on inner surface of symphysis pubis; measures 10 cm.
The obstetric conjugate represents the shortest diameter traversed by the fetal head during inlet engagement.
Diagonal conjugate: Midpoint of sacral promontory to lower border of symphysis pubis; measures 12.5 cm.
Obstetric conjugate cannot be measured directly; it is calculated by subtracting 1.5 to 2 cm from diagonal conjugate.
In digital pelvimetry, inability of the middle finger to reach the sacral promontory confirms an adequate inlet.

groups.label: Transverse and oblique diameters
bullets: Transverse diameter of inlet: Between the two farthest points on the iliopectineal line; measures 13 cm.
Right oblique diameter: From right sacroiliac joint to left iliopectineal eminence; measures 12 cm.
Left oblique diameter: From left sacroiliac joint to right iliopectineal eminence; measures 12 cm.
Sacrocotyloid diameter: From tip of sacral promontory to corresponding iliopectineal eminence; measures 9.5 cm.

blocks.title: The pelvic cavity
bullets: Segment bounded above by the pelvic brim and below by the plane of least pelvic dimensions.
Bounded anteriorly by the posterior pubic symphysis and posteriorly by the hollow curvature of the sacrum.
Circular in configuration, measuring approximately 12 cm across all planes (anteroposterior and transverse).
Plane of greatest pelvic dimension: Roomiest plane running from mid-inner pubic symphysis to S2-S3 sacral junction and mid-acetabulum.
Sacrosciatic notch is wide and shallow with straight, divergent sidewalls in gynaecoid and anthropoid pelves.
Sacrosciatic notch is narrow and deep with convergent sidewalls (funnelling) in the android pelvis.

blocks.title: The pelvic outlet and its boundaries

groups.label: Obstetrical outlet
bullets: Bounded above by plane of least pelvic dimensions (ischial spines) and below by anatomical outlet.
Bounded anteriorly by lower border of pubic symphysis, posteriorly by coccyx, and laterally by ischial spines.

groups.label: Anatomical outlet
bullets: Diamond-shaped bony and ligamentous boundary forming the pelvic base.
Bounded anteriorly by lower border of pubic symphysis, anterolaterally by ischiopubic rami and ischial tuberosities.
Bounded posteromedially by sacrotuberous and sacrospinous ligaments, and posteriorly by tip of the coccyx.
The anatomical outlet is of minor obstetric significance compared to the obstetrical outlet.

blocks.title: Diameters and axes of the pelvic outlet

groups.label: Outlet diameters
bullets: Obstetric anteroposterior diameter: From lower border of pubic symphysis to tip of the sacrum; measures 13 cm.
Anatomical anteroposterior diameter: From lower border of pubic symphysis to tip of the coccyx; measures 11 cm.
Bituberous diameter: Between inner margins of the ischial tuberosities; measures 11 cm.
Bispinous diameter: Between tips of ischial spines; measures 10.5 cm; represents narrowest pelvic diameter.
Posterior sagittal diameter: From tip of sacrum to midpoint of bituberous line; measures 7.5 to 10 cm.
Anterior sagittal diameter: From lower border of pubic symphysis to midpoint of bituberous line; measures 6 to 7 cm.

groups.label: Subpubic arch and waste space
bullets: Subpubic angle measures approximately 90 degrees in the gynaecoid pelvis; rounded arch wastes minimal space.
A narrow pubic arch displaces the descending fetal crown backwards, impeding vaginal birth.
Waste space of Morris is the clearance between subpubic arch and flexed fetal crown; normally does not exceed 1 cm.

groups.label: Pelvic axes
bullets: Obstetric axis is J-shaped: Passes downward and backward along inlet axis to ischial spines, then downward and forward along outlet.
Anatomical axis (curve of Carus) is C-shaped with forward concavity, joining midpoints of inlet, cavity, and outlet.

blocks.title: Clinical significance of the level of ischial spines
bullets: Demarcates the plane of the obstetric outlet (plane of least pelvic dimensions).
Represents the narrowest transverse dimension of the pelvis (bispinous diameter measuring 10.5 cm).
Site where the obstetric axis of descent curves from downward-backward to downward-forward.
Anatomical attachment of the levator ani muscle (ischiococcygeus portion).
Exact plane where internal rotation of the fetal head occurs during labour.
Landmark for fetal head engagement: Vault felt vaginally at or below this level establishes engagement.
Landmark for transvaginal pudendal nerve block administration.
Corresponds to the anatomical level of the external cervical os.
Designated as station 0: Levels above are scored negative (-1 to -3) and levels below are scored positive (+1 to +3).
Level of the normal vaginal vault; descent below this plane represents vault prolapse.
Retention shelf for ring pessaries: Pessaries must sit above this level for conservative prolapse management.
Absolute boundary for operative vaginal delivery: Obstetric forceps is never applied above this level.

viva.q: How is the obstetric conjugate calculated clinically and why is it important?
viva.a: It is calculated by subtracting 1.5 to 2 cm from the diagonal conjugate (12.5 cm - 2 cm = 10.5 cm or 10 cm). It is the narrowest inlet diameter the head traverses.

viva.q: What is the clinical significance of the ischial spines in assessing station?
viva.a: The ischial spines represent station zero. Descent above is designated as -1 to -3 cm, while descent below is +1 to +3 cm, marking fetal head engagement.

viva.q: What is the waste space of Morris and what is its normal limit?
viva.a: It is the distance between the subpubic arch and the descending fetal crown. Normally it should not exceed 1 cm; a narrow arch increases this space, forcing the head backward.

viva.q: What are the shapes of the pelvic inlet in the four Caldwell-Moloy pelvic types?
viva.a: Gynaecoid is rounded, anthropoid is longitudinally oval, android is triangular or heart-shaped, and platypelloid is transversely flat or oval.
